The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{15\sqrt{3}}{2}{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Determine $m∠A.$
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=5\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC=6\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $m∠A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{15\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 6\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{15\sqrt{3}}{2} & =15\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{\cancel{15}\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\cancel{15}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡A & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ m∠A & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
